title: Fleet Command
description: See how Star Atlas expands from personal-scale immersion into a larger strategic command layer with territory, logistics, and faction operations.
heroTitle: From pilot fantasy to admiral thinking.
heroSummary: Fleet Command matters because it changes the scale of your decisions. The redesign treats it as a strategic layer with a clear role in the broader universe, not just a side mode.
utilityLine: This page clarifies where command-scale play sits inside the Star Atlas product stack.

heroMedia.label: Command preview
heroMedia.caption: Scale is only compelling when the player understands what changes at that scale.

heroPanel.title: Fleet Command turns scale into a different kind of mastery.
heroPanel.body: The page now makes it clear that command play is about coordination, resource leverage, and territorial decision-making rather than simply zooming the camera out.

sections.heading: What changes when the player steps into the operational layer.

cards.title: See the board
cards.body: Strategic overview reveals supply, movement, territory, and threat in ways cockpit play cannot.

cards.title: Move more than one asset
cards.body: Fleet-level play creates a richer sense of responsibility, planning, and timing.

cards.title: Hold valuable space
cards.body: Territory only matters when it is defended, contested, and logistically supported.

sections.heading: Strategic scale is one of the reasons Star Atlas feels bigger than a typical sci-fi game pitch.
body: This page now makes the argument directly: Fleet Command is where the universe starts to feel like a living power map instead of a series of isolated moments.
The design keeps the message lean so the ambition feels believable instead of overpromised.
sections.asideTitle: Clarity matters more than inflated status language.
sections.asideBody: The page avoids speculative countdowns and cluttered utility states, focusing on the strategic promise in clear terms.

items.question: Why is Fleet Command important to the marketing story?
items.answer: Because it signals scale and depth. It tells the visitor that Star Atlas is not only about a single avatar perspective.

items.question: What is the right next step from here?
items.answer: See the roadmap for product status clarity or move into the economy page to understand what command decisions are ultimately protecting and amplifying.

finalCta.title: Follow command scale into economy and roadmap context.
finalCta.text: See the systems that make command meaningful, then track how the product is framed going forward.
